chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered that tawaf be performed on behalf of one afflicted with an abdominal illness and one with a fracture; meaning that one in such a condition also has tawaf performed on his behalf only when he has been waited for some days, then does not recover, and missing it is feared; in that case, it is permissible that tawaf be performed on his behalf. This indicates that.

key_terms.الْفَوْتُ: missing the rite or losing the opportunity
key_terms.الْكَسِيرِ: one suffering from a fracture or broken limb
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونِ: one afflicted with an abdominal illness

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for tawaf to be performed on behalf of a sick or injured person?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning tawaf for a sick or injured person who is unable to perform it personally. It indicates that if recovery is awaited for some days but does not occur and the time may be missed, then it is permissible for tawaf to be performed on that person's behalf.
